notes: Instrumentation task — no register proposals (the bundle's claims: []). T514/F5: the logjam-flag lifecycle in tools/fleet-keeper.sh. THE DEFECT (from the 2026-08-20 fleet-and-model audit, docs/audits/2026-08-20-fleet-and-model-audit.md F5): untracked/fleet-keeper.logjam.flag was written by the keeper once a blocked anchor waited past FLEET_LOGJAM_FLAG minutes, but was never removed when pressure exited — the audit found the flag naming T364 waited=241min while pressure.json said NORMAL and T364 was RUNNING. A loud artifact that outlives its condition trains readers to ignore it. THE FIX (committed as d5397ac, 'Recover T514/T517/T518 worker code from the tree, validate it, make its regression sh-portable'): the flag is now written ONLY by the pressure state machine (anchor != null AND waited >= FLEET_LOGJAM_FLAG minutes, setting `flagged = True`) and is reconciled to the current pressure state every iteration — after the pressure block, `if not flagged and os.path.exists(LOGJAM_FLAG): os.remove(...)` clears it the iteration the condition no longer holds: pressure exit (anchor null), re-anchor to a different id (fresh waiting_since below threshold), or defensively the same anchor dropping below threshold (unreachable while the anchor stays, since waited only grows, but correct regardless). A flag the keeper did not write — hand-planted, or a leftover from a crashed previous run — is swept by the keeper's own cleanup on the next iteration the condition is false, not by a manual `rm` (never hand-planted, never left stale). Telemetry only: clearing the flag dispatches nothing and never preempts a holder (the one-writer invariant, §3 of the design). Under cooldown the flag is left untouched — main() early-returns on cooldown_set() (tools/fleet-keeper.sh ~line 374) before the pressure/flag section, so cooldown pauses pressure without resetting it; the flag is reconciled when cooldown lifts. PROVENANCE: the code was written by the previously dispatched worker (glm-5.2, per the commit message) and recovered/validated/committed by the incoming Orchestrator seat; this row was healed back to dispatchable for the findings deliverable only — the bundle amendment explicitly says the code is already written, validated, and committed and must not be rewritten; the file's `holds` was released for exactly that reason and no source edit was needed or made by this worker.
